subject: Midline OKR brief: scope adjustments, blockers, and dependency asks
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Midline OKR brief: scope adjustments, blockers, and dependency asks

Team —

Quick midline note ahead of next week's leadership check: overall health on our Serving Economics objective is mixed and requires 1) a small scope shift and 2) two short dependency commitments to hit QBR targets. Summary below — full slide deck attached.

TL;DR
- Net: We expect to be ~65% to target on Unit Cost reduction by quarter end unless we accept a scoped defer for non-essential quantization work.
- Ask #1 (Infra): Temporary 2-week Dedicated capacity bump (2x A100-equivalent) to complete end-to-end perf runs for the 512-token profile.
- Ask #2 (Sales/Product): Extended evaluation window with Pinecrest (they're in procurement) — need committed POC support to validate latency SLOs for their production profile.

What changed since planning
- Production traffic shape skewed higher on 512 token requests (unexpected), increasing per-token cost in our current batching profile.
- The quantization experiment that should lower cost by 15% is delayed because the kernels need a second pass for stability on Ampere; this is an engineering 2‑week blocker.

Proposal (recommended)
1) De-scope: Move non-critical model pruning experiments to next quarter (keeps the quantization effort focused).
2) Infra bump: Request temporary Dedicated allocation for perf runs and real-traffic soak. Estimated cost in attachment.
3) Customer support: Assign a named SE for Pinecrest procurement window next week (their test harness is fragile; a hands-on week shortens procurement by ~3 workweeks).

Specific asks 
- Vanessa: Can you authorize the Dedicated bump (see capacity_estimates_q3.xlsx) and surface any billing/commit concerns to Finance? I tagged the cost estimate with both a conservative and aggressive scenario.
- Karthik: Can your team prioritize the kernel stability pass (two engineers, max 2 weeks)? If not possible, confirm timeline so we can communicate alternate options to the customer.
- Marissa: Can CS commit to a 1-week dedicated POC cadence for Pinecrest starting Sep 27? I tentatively penciled Lydia Chen on the calendar — she wants a live run.

Attachments: QBR_pulse_deck_v2.pdf (slides); capacity_estimates_q3.xlsx (numbers).

Thanks — I want to be candid in the QBR: this is recoverable with the two asks above but we'll need clear commitments. I'll synthesize a 1-slide exec-ready summary once I have replies.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
VP, Serving & Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Midline OKR brief: scope adjustments, blockers, and dependency asks

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear runbook. I support the proposed de-scope and agree the infra bump is the fastest path to validated numbers for QBR. I have two items:

1) Billing guardrails: Finance needs a short note that the bump is temporary (two weeks) and that we will attach the cost to the Serving R&D bucket for now. I can draft that note if you want.
2) Prioritization trade: The Dedicated bump will impact available capacity for other teams if we take the aggressive scenario. Can you confirm the absolute minimum capacity for the perf runs? If it's the conservative case we may be able to green-light without broader impact.

I'll loop in Finance if you can confirm the minimum slot size. Once confirmed, I'll send an approval email and mark it high priority.

-Vanessa
Director, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Midline OKR brief: scope adjustments, blockers, and dependency asks

Raf / Vanessa —

We can staff the kernel stability pass, but to avoid context switching I recommend a 1-week focused spike first (one senior perf engineer + one engineer). If the spike is promising we extend to week two. That gets us a quick go/no-go for the quantization path and should produce telemetry we can share in the QBR.

I'll block Mudit and Leila for Mon-Tue next week for the spike. Rafael, can you share the perf harness link (or point to the Drive folder) so they can prep?

-Karthik
Engineering Director, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia@pinecrest.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Midline OKR brief: scope adjustments, blockers, and dependency asks

Rafael / all —

Pinecrest confirmed they can move their POC window up if we provide SE support the week of Sep 27. Procurement asked for a short technical runbook and an estimated SLO table to attach to their contract (I'll draft). Attaching initial notes in the deck; will add the SLO table by Monday.

Lydia — thanks for the flexibility. We'll propose 3 live-run slots and one soak window; let me know which days work best.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Sep 27, 2026 at 09:00 AM Lydia Chen <lydia@pinecrest.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — the earlier support is ideal. We prefer Tue/Wed for the live runs.
> — Lydia
